assertion_independence: No added assertion compares a value against the variable the test handed in: the byte allowance is the done-when's own fixture constant, the record counters assert only that the instrument saw something, and both summary comparisons take their other side from a fresh read of the file (tests/test_the_parsed_stream_cache_keeps_what_the_next_pass_asks_for.py:122 and :265) rather than from the cache's own report. The one input taken from the code under test is the truncated-stream case's `state`, read from observe_log at :237 and passed back as `resume`; the compared outputs still come from the file's own lines, so a broken state carry would not make that assertion hold.

assertion_reviews.failure_condition: Shrinking STREAM_COUNT or STREAM_BYTES below the 32 MB bound reddens it, so the case cannot pass vacuously over a population the bound already holds.

Any second pass that re-parses a stream from its first byte reddens it; negative-control-base.log records 125,562,900 B against the 36,000 B allowance with `1 failed` and EXIT=1 at b3a277e1, and the counter is taken at the parse boundary rather than read back from the cache.
A cache that answers the second pass with no parse at all reddens it, which stops the byte allowance passing by answering nothing.

A resumed summary that drops the records before its cursor, or folds the append twice, disagrees with observe_stream over lines the test read from the file itself (line 136), so the other side of the comparison is not produced by the code under test.

assertion_reviews.assertion: assert [event['message']['id'] for event in whole] == [f'msg_{index:06d}' for index in range(43)]
assertion_reviews.failure_condition: A whole request answered from a tail entry reddens it; negative-control-repairs.log records exactly that answer (msg_000040..msg_000042) at the mutation that removes the whole flag from both early returns.

A resume that seeks past a truncated stream's end and returns the carried state reddens it; the cited log shows that failure, but against an earlier revision's test text (see the finding at line 265).
Re-reading the held stream on a whole request reddens it; negative-control-join.log records 17,673 B against the 1,236 B it gained.

assertion_reviews.assertion: assert (events, malformed) == (whole, whole_malformed) or any((events, malformed) == (gained[start:], 0) for start in range(len(gained)))
assertion_reviews.failure_condition: An answer carrying a record the worker did not append, repeating one, or answering with no records reddens it; a suffix starting past the read's true boundary, including one missing the earliest appended record, passes (see the finding at tests/test_watch_stream_parse_is_cached.py:240).

findings.text: non-blocking: `resume = grows and (joined or not whole)` is the only place the summary cursor answers a read, and it needs whole=False, which no production caller passes - reckon/_backends.py:4658, reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1197 and reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:837 all pass whole=True - so the delivery s88 names (a steady tick re-parses only streams that grew) is unchanged at this head: the run's own RCA records the tick row at 12,084 B at both revisions and the unfolded-reader row at 126.8 MB at head, so closing s88 on this head would record the 42.7% census row as addressed when it is not. This repeats a non-blocking finding of the reviews at faef3e5499 and 1a015d15eb, now measurable: the first-ranked reader gains only the whole-entry join.

non-blocking: `_StreamCursor.as_resume` has no caller - a search for the name over the head tree returns one occurrence, its own definition - so an accessor added beside the resume work is dead code in the module the census ranks first.

non-blocking: line 550 names `cached_stream_events` "the census's first-ranked reader: it is entered for a reader the summary has not folded yet, and by observe_log's own fallback", and the table under it credits that reader with 126,806,578 B -> 12,296 B; at this head the fallback at reckon/_backends.py:4658 passes whole=True, so the production entry lands on the 126.8 MB row rather than the 12,296 B row the paragraph attributes to it.

non-blocking: the widened disjunction accepts `(events, malformed) == (gained[start:], 0)` for any start, so a resumed answer that drops the earliest records a worker appended still passes; the exact comparison against the whole read that this replaces was the guard, and negative-control-dropped-record.log reddens only because that instance answered with no records at all.

non-blocking: the truncated-stream case's cited negative control (negative-control-resume-bound.log, named on the reviewed manifest's negative_control_note line 26) was captured against test text calling `_backends._STREAM_CURSORS.clear()` and `_backends._PARSED_STREAM_LOCK`, a store this head does not carry (a search for `_STREAM_CURSORS` over reckon/_backends.py at 1b6e2253 returns nothing), so that red is not this head's guard; the guard it names is present at reckon/_backends.py:4643 (`cursor.offset <= info.st_size`) but no head-revision log shows it refusing.

non-blocking: the reviewed run's manifest `tests:` line omits tests/test_watch_stream_parse_is_cached.py while its own `after_suite` command and after-suite-local.log's `# command:` header both carry it and the log's summary reads `65 passed`; promotion fills its gate receipt from the `tests:` line, so the receipt would cite a command that was not the head arm this run measured.
